narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>Multiply all five bottom numbers together and use that as the common bottom number.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It would work, but the number is huge, and every top number grows with it.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We want the smallest common bottom number, so that slip is struck.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble shows the five bottoms multiplied to a very long number; the long number runs off the edge of the working band; the slip's bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Find the lowest common multiple of the bottoms by primes, then change every fraction to it.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Add the tops and write the answer over the common bottom number.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>When the top equals the bottom, the five bowls fill the pot exactly.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the words smallest common bottom number by primes, then add the tops appear; the check that the five bowls fill exactly one pot is shown with a tick

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip multiplies all five bottom numbers to get a huge common bottom number. It works, but the numbers are very large, and the lowest common multiple is much smaller.
